verdict.reasoning: Patient reports right knee pain and clicking and intermittent tingling in toes: “now my knees are hurting, and they're clicking a lot…”, later clarifies “it's actually my right knee that hurts” and “there was tingling in my toes like on my… right toes.”
Onset: Doctor asks “when do you think it started?” Patient: “probably, it's been about two weeks.”

Context and distances: “I'm currently training for a marathon… I'm actually not even doing such long runs, maybe like seven or eight miles… I started about uh, maybe a month ago… I've done like… four or five miles, and I've just done like a couple of seven, mile runs.”

Timing and effect on running: “I would say probably starts off like after, uh, maybe, twenty minutes or so… and… the last time I actually stopped… then I stopped, because it was… I, I feel like it's getting worse.”
Clicking with flexion to extension: “when I start doing my abs… to kind of go from the flex position on my knees, and straighten my legs, then I feel all this clicking.”
Location: “I feel it in the middle, but I almost feel like maybe it kind of… moves to the right, to the right of my knee a little bit.” (central with slight lateral/right component).
Swelling history: “it did, like, the first time I ran, it was a little bit swollen, but then I just put some like ice on it, and it went away… right now it's not swollen.”

Function and stability: Patient denies giving way and locking: “Not, not bad, I mean it just kinda starts hurting”, “Any locking up of the knee?… No.” “Any problems going up and down stairs? Patient: No.” “Any problems just walking normally? Patient: No.” “Are you able to fully straighten the leg? Patient: Yes. … fully flex it? Patient: Yes.”
Single episode toe tingling: “there was this tingling in my toes… after the run… on my… right toes” and later “No it was just, it was that time… it kind of went on for a while.”
Hyperopia: “I mean I, I do have, I'm far-sighted, and so I had uh, I had Lasik surgery.” (far-sighted = hyperopic).
LASIK: “I do have, I'm far-sighted, and so I had uh, I had Lasik surgery.”
Severe UTI with ER visit, concern for kidney stones: “once I had this really bad UTI, they thought it was kidney stones, and so they had me actually in ER.”
Ice-hockey injury: “I play some ice hockey, and I had this injury a few months ago… I just like, fell on the ice and… had a, huge bruise.”
Ibuprofen use and dose: “Yes I , I take Ibuprofen… So I'll take Ibuprofen for that… it's nothing like major maybe, like, four hundred milligrams max, something like that.”
Aleve as needed: “Sometimes, you know, just for cramps, I'll take, like… ibuprofen, or actually , uh, I'll take, what am I taking? Aleve.”
Vitamin D: “Well, I'll take uh, I take vitamin D.”
Melatonin: “I take melatonin… I prefer Melatonin, it's just sometimes Melatonin doesn't work.”
Xanax PRN for sleep: “You know occasionally, if I'm really having hard times, like I'll, I'll sleeping, I'll take Xanax.”
Activity level and marathon training: “I play a lot of sports… I'm currently training for a marathon.”
Cannabis use: “I also sometimes will um, you know, smoke a joint.”

Summary matches details: right knee pain with activity and clicking for ~2 weeks (“it's been about two weeks”), in marathon training context, no instability or locking (“No” to giving way and locking), transient swelling (“first time I ran, it was a little bit swollen… went away”), and one transient right toe tingling episode (“there was tingling… on my… right toes… it was just that time”).
Rest and not running through pain: “I would, try and ease up on the running, if you can. And if it, if it's painful enough that you're, having to stop running, then it's not a good idea, to do that.”
Continue icing: “definitely carrying on with the ice therapy that you've been using… as much as you can, use the ice.”

Stronger NSAID replacing Ibuprofen, with food and not together: “It's fine to take the Ibuprofen. Um, I can prescribe you a slightly stronger, anti-inflammatory that you can take regularly instead of the Ibuprofen, but not with the Ibuprofen. But make sure that with food.”

Physio referral placed: “the best thing I would, suggest, getting a appointment with the physiotherapist first…”, and when asked “are you going to send referral for that?” Doctor: “Yep, we can, we can do a referral before that.”

Imaging considered based on physio/ongoing concerns: “then we can make an assessment as to whether we need to do any, um, imagery to , have a look inside the knee, and see if there's any problem with the, cartilage.”

Safety netting: “If in the meantime you develop like persistant swelling, heat, redness, um, of the knee, or high temperature, feel unwell, or it completely locks up and you can't bend and stretch it… then, you'd need to see a doctor urgently, so call us back in that, case.”
Follow-up in clinic if physio wait is long: “the, a physio is the best point of call… But certainly if the appointment time's too long to wait, then we can see, we can see you in our clinic as well.”
